4. The learned Munsif decreed the suit on contest. On appeal by the defendant-petitioners the appellate court below dismissed the suit on the finding that the land of the suit Khatian being C.S. Khatian No. 26 was auction-sold and Karam Sheikh purchased the same and defendant Nos. 5-10 as well as the heirs of Karam Sheikh purchased the suit land from him and also from his subsequent purchasers. 

 5. The plaintiff-respondents thereafter moved the High Court Division in revision and obtained rule. Subsequently the High Court Division made the rule absolute concurring with the finding of the learned Munsif that the defendants produced no documentary or oral evidence in respect of the money decree dated 8.1.1923 obtained in the money suit filed by Karam Sheikh and that there as an auction-sale of the land of the suit Khatian pursuant to the said decree and Karam Sheikh purchased the land of the suit Khatian in auction and dismissed the suit on the ground that the defendants' claim of title and possession in the suit land was not proved. The High Court Division also held that the court of appeal below dis-missed the suit as not maintainable without discussing the evidence and thus made the rule absolute. 

 6. Leave was granted to consider whether the High Court Division erred in failing to hold that Karam Ali Sheikh purchased the suit land in auction in Money Execution Case No.183 of 1923 and sale certificate was issued on 7.1.1924 which was marked as exhibit and he subsequently obtained possession of the suit land through court. Whether the High court Division also erred in dismissing the suit in failing to consider. Exhibits D,E,F,H,I,J,K and L which point to the fact that the suit C.S. Khatian was sold in auction and was purchased by Karam Ali Sheikh which was subsequently purchased by the defendants and the heirs of original C.S. recorded tenant Kurban Ali although this was duly considered and discussed by the court of appeal below. 

 10. It is noted on careful perusal and examination of the materials on record that the land of the suit Khatian was sold in auction in the aforesaid money execution case arising out of the said money suit filed by Karam Sheikh against the heirs of Kurban Ali and Karam Sheikh auction purchased the land of the suit Khatian and the defendants purchased the suit land from Karam Shikh as well as his heirs. Karam Sheikh also sold some land of the suit Khatian to the plaintiffs who are heirs of Kurban Ali, the original owner of the land of the suit Khatian. The defendants proved the sale certificate which was marked as exhibit in the suit. The defendants have also succeeded in proving the sale of the land of the suit Khatian to the defendants, plaintiffs   as heirs of Kurban Ali and also to others by proving the sale deeds and other documents including the rent receipts showing possession of the defendants in the suit land vide Exhts. D, E, F, H, I, J, K and L. Despite such proof the trial Court as well as the High Court Division decreed the suit by finding title and possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs without considering the aforesaid exhibits. As a result there has been a miscarriage of justice.
